title: The "1-hour" Black Friday banner
context:
It's Wednesday, day 6 of the sprint. Sophie messages you:

> *"Can you add a Black Friday **countdown banner** to the homepages of all three brands by tomorrow? Our agency says it's 1 hour of work. Thanks!"*

You check with Priya (tech lead):
- The homepages have **CMS content slots**: the content team can publish a **static image banner** today, no developers needed.
- A **live countdown timer** is a **new component**: about 3 days including NL/FR translations, QA on three brands and regression.
- The **code freeze starts Friday 18:00**.
- The sprint goal is *"Shoppers on Chemist & Co can reserve an item and get a confirmation."* The team has no slack.
task: Decide how to handle the request, reply to Sophie, and note what you would raise at the retrospective.
constraints: Protect the sprint goal and the bug fix
Keep the reply short enough for a chat message

options.label: Accept it into the sprint: it's only an hour
options.feedback: The "hour" is the agency's guess. The real work is 3 days and it would break the sprint goal before the freeze.

options.label: Decline: nothing new enters a running sprint
options.feedback: Too rigid. There is a no-developer option that meets most of the need today.

options.label: Clarify the need, offer the static CMS banner via the content team today, and only if the live countdown is essential, agree openly what drops out
options.feedback: Helpful and protects the goal: the BU gets a banner today; any trade-off is explicit.

options.label: Ask two developers to build it in overtime tonight
options.feedback: Rushed work right before a freeze is risky, and overtime hides the real cost.

parts.label: For the retrospective
parts.prompt: What would you raise at the retro so this goes better next time?

keypoints.label: Offers the CMS/static banner via the content team
Mentions the real size from the tech lead

rubric.full: Explores the no-developer option and makes trade-offs explicit
rubric.partial: Right direction, missing the alternative or the trade-off

rubric.full: Real size, freeze date, goal impact
Short, friendly, ends with a clear next step

rubric.criterion: Protects the sprint goal and bug fix
rubric.full: Explicit about what must not move

hints: Separate the need (a visible Black Friday message by tomorrow) from the solution (a live countdown component).
Is there a way to meet most of the need without developers? Who else can publish to the homepage?

Reply structure: thanks + the need you heard → what you checked (3 days, freeze Friday) → offer: static CMS banner today → if the countdown is essential, what would drop out → question to confirm. Retro: a campaign calendar so requests arrive two sprints ahead.
modelAnswer:
**Decision:** clarify and offer the CMS option; only bring the countdown in with an explicit trade-off.

**Reply**
> Hi Sophie, thanks. I get that you need Black Friday visible on all homepages tomorrow. I checked with Priya: a **static banner** can go live **today** through the content team's CMS slots, no developers needed. A **live countdown** is a new component: about 3 days with translations and QA on three brands, and the code freeze starts Friday 18:00. Building it would mean dropping the Reserve & Collect confirmation email from this sprint. Would the static banner work for you? If the countdown is essential, let's agree today what moves out.

**Retro:** set up a shared **campaign calendar** with the BUs so campaign needs reach refinement at least two sprints ahead, and agree a small "fast lane" for content-only changes.
commonMistakes: Believing the "1 hour" estimate from someone outside the team
A flat "no" without offering the CMS route
Quietly squeezing it in and failing the sprint goal
A reply that is a wall of process text
